Getting around

Buy a 24/48/72-hour pass and use the U-Bahn and trams; the centre is flat and walkable.

  • ✓Metro ★U-Bahn, trams and buses share one ticket. Buy a 24/48/72-hour pass or single fares around €2.60. Validate before riding; inspectors fine on the spot.
  • ✓BusBuses and trams use the same ticket as the U-Bahn. Validate before riding.
  • ✓Taxi / ride appsTaxis are metered. Uber and Bolt both work in Vienna.
  • ✓Rental carDriving is slow and parking is scarce. Skip the rental car in town.
  • ✓Walking ★The centre is flat and walkable. Bikes and e-scooters are easy to rent.
  • ✗FerryNo ferries. The Danube is crossed by bridges and the U-Bahn.
Recommended stay★ 3 nights (4 days)

Three nights covers the big palaces, two or three museums and a proper café afternoon without rushing.

Climate

Continental climate: cold winters, warm summers, and rain spread through the year. Spring and autumn are the easiest months to walk the city.

  • 🌸Best months: April to June and SeptemberHighs around 16–26°C. Comfortable for walking and palaces without summer heat.
  • ☀️Summer is warm, not extremeJuly and August peak near 27°C with mild nights around 17°C. Some afternoons feel humid.
  • ❄️Winter is properly coldDecember to February highs of 4–6°C and lows near or below freezing. Snow is possible but not guaranteed.
  • 🌧️Rain all yearAbout 7–13 rain days every month, most in May. Showers often pass; a small umbrella is enough.
  • 🧥Pack layersA warm coat and gloves for November to March; light layers and a rain jacket for spring and autumn.
  • 🎄December is festive but coldChristmas markets are outdoors. Wear boots and thermals, and warm up in coffee houses.

Landmarks 33

Must-see · 8

  1. 1

    Schönbrunn Palace

    The Habsburgs' summer residence is Vienna's most visited sight, with grand state rooms and vast gardens. Book a timed ticket online to skip the queue, and go early morning to beat the crowds.

  2. 2

    Hofburg Palace

    The sprawling imperial palace in the city center housed the Habsburg court for centuries. Visit the imperial apartments and the Sisi Museum, and note the complex is a short walk from the U3 Herrengasse stop.

  3. 3

    St Stephen's Cathedral

    The Gothic cathedral with its patterned roof is the heart of the old town. Climb the south tower for views or take the lift up the north tower; entry to the nave is free but towers are ticketed.

  4. 4

    Belvedere Palace

    The baroque palace houses Austrian art including Klimt's The Kiss. Buy tickets online and allow time for the gardens between the Upper and Lower palaces.

  5. 5

    Vienna State Opera

    One of the world's great opera houses, central to Vienna's musical identity. Standing-room tickets are sold cheaply on the day, and guided tours run when there is no rehearsal.

  6. 6

    Kunsthistorisches Museum

    A world-class art museum in a magnificent building on the Ringstrasse. Go on a weekday morning for quieter galleries, and don't miss the Kunstkammer collection.

  7. 7

    MuseumsQuartier

    A lively cultural quarter with major museums, courtyards and outdoor seating. It's a good base for an afternoon, with the Leopold Museum and mumok on site.

  8. 8

    Naschmarkt

    Vienna's best-known market, with produce stalls, spices and casual eateries. Come on a weekday morning; Saturdays are busy and the flea market runs on Saturdays.

    ★★★☆☆ · Half day · 33 km from Vienna

    Best way: Frequent direct S-Bahn trains reach Baden in 21 minutes, far faster than the 59-minute bus.

    Frequent direct suburban trains (S-Bahn) run from Vienna to Baden bei Wien in well under an hour.

    • Train ★21 min · from $1-$10
    • Bus59 min · from $8-$12
    • Car34 min · taxi ≈ €60

    What to see

    • Baden spa and casino
    • Kaiserhaus and pedestrian center
    • Rosarium and Kurpark
    • Nearby vineyards and Helenental

    Good to know

    • Baden is a spa town with thermal baths and a pedestrian old town
    • Best visited in spring through early autumn for the gardens and outdoor spa

    Wiener Neustadt · 30 min by train

    ★★☆☆☆ · Half day · 58 km from Vienna

    Best way: Direct regional trains take just 30 minutes, much better than the 48-minute drive.

    Frequent direct regional trains run from Vienna's main station to Wiener Neustadt in about 45 minutes.

    • Train ★30 min · from €21
    • Car48 min · taxi ≈ €100

    What to see

    • Main square and town hall
    • Dom of Wiener Neustadt
    • Theresian Military Academy
    • Nearby Schneeberg foothills

    Good to know

    • The old town and main square are a short walk from the station
    • The Theresian Military Academy and cathedral are the main sights

    Build my plan

    Swap in instead

    • Swap a museum morning for Schönbrunn Palace and its gardens, half a day with the U4.
    • Take a day trip to the Wachau valley or Baden by train; check times on the day.
    • Add a Danube evening: swim or walk at the Alte Donau, or cycle the Donauinsel.

    Getting around

    • U-Bahn, trams, and buses run on one ticket; buy a 24/48/72-hour pass or single fares around €2.60.
    • Validate tickets before riding; inspectors fine on the spot.
    • Taxis are metered; Uber and Bolt both work in Vienna.
    • Driving is slow and parking is scarce; skip the rental car in town.
    • The centre is flat and walkable; bikes and e-scooters are easy to rent.
    • No ferries; the Danube is crossed by bridges and the U-Bahn.

    Where to stay

    • Innere Stadt · ≈ EUR 150–400 a night
      Walk to St. Stephen's, the Hofburg and the Ringstrasse. Quietest at night; book early.
    • Leopoldstadt · ≈ EUR 90–220 a night
      Across the Danube canal, near the Prater and the Augarten. Good U-Bahn links, better value.
    • Mariahilf · ≈ EUR 100–240 a night
      Between the MuseumsQuartier and the Naschmarkt. Lively streets, easy walk to the centre.
    • Neubau · ≈ EUR 85–200 a night
      Independent shops, bars and cafés. Young feel, 10–15 minutes on the U-Bahn to the centre.

    Food & drink

    • Try a Wiener Schnitzel (veal or pork) with potato salad, and Tafelspitz (boiled beef) in a traditional Beisl.
    • Coffee houses are a ritual: order a Melange, sit long, and read the papers. Cake like Sachertorte or Apfelstrudel is normal mid-afternoon.
    • Naschmarkt on Saturday morning: stalls, spices and cheap snacks. Many stands close on Sunday.
    • Street food: a Käsekrainer sausage from a Würstelstand, around €5–7.
    • Book dinner ahead for popular places; many kitchens close around 22:00. Tipping is rounding up plus a little, said aloud.

    Tips

    1. Coffeehouse culture is sacred — order a Melange, take your time, and don't expect the waiter to rush you
    2. Buy a multi-day transit pass, but remember to validate it before your first ride
    3. Tap water is exceptionally clean and comes directly from springs in the Alps
    4. Almost all retail stores, including grocery shops, are strictly closed on Sundays
    5. Stand on the right, walk on the left on all subway escalators

    Souvenirs

    Original Sacher-Torte

    EUR 72–921 piece (small size) · shop prices

    A chocolate cake with apricot jam, and Vienna's most famous cake. It was created at the Hotel Sacher in the 19th century.

    Where: Café Sacher official shop
    Check the official packaging, size, shelf life, and shipping terms before you buy.

    Augarten espresso cup

    EUR 140–2001 cup · shop prices

    Handmade porcelain from Vienna's historic Augarten manufactory, known for fine craftsmanship.

    Where: Augarten Porzellan main store, Obere Augartenstraße
    Ask whether the saucer is included.

    Mozart Kugeln

    EUR 8–251 box · estimate

    Chocolate-covered pralines with marzipan and nougat, named after the composer Mozart, who is closely linked to Vienna.

    Where: Café Demel
